choice.purpose: Let Sunny pick how she wants to build speed and confidence on her weak words before the independent checkpoint, since either path gives equivalent targeted retrieval practice.
choice.label: Choose your practice adventure

options.label: Arcade Speed Path
options.hypothesis: Sunny engages longer and retrieves weak words faster when practice is wrapped in timed arcade competition (monster-stampede, letter-rush).

options.label: Puzzle Strategy Path
options.hypothesis: Sunny engages longer and reasons through letter patterns more carefully when practice is wrapped in a puzzle format (wordle, wheel-of-fortune).

options.label: Adverbs made from adjectives ending in -ow/-ick/-ick+ly keep the full base word + ly (slow+ly, quick+ly)
It's just memorized with no pattern
Double 'm' in the middle, common pattern in many 2-syllable words
It ends in -er like a comparison word

measurement.supportCriteria: Child watches/interacts with chunk explanations for the 4 words missed on discovery baseline (slowly, quickly, common, remember) before any recall practice begins.
measurement.reviseCriteria: If child cannot articulate the chunk pattern back in the embedded check rounds, flag for re-teaching before moving to recall practice.
measurement.falsifyCriteria: This is exposure only; it does not by itself predict test accuracy and must not be treated as evidence of spelling ability.

spelling.reason: These 4 words were independently missed on the fresh discovery checkpoint (slowly->slowle, quickly->quickle, common->commne, remember->remembre), so they need direct chunk-pattern teaching before further recall practice.
spelling.uncertainty: Visual exposure does not confirm the child can produce the word unaided; teachability only.

activities.title: Hear It, Spell It: Letter Recall Warm-Up

measurement.supportCriteria: Word hidden during response; child hears word spoken then spells letter-by-letter with letter-box scaffolding, after the chunk teaching above.
measurement.reviseCriteria: If 3+ of these 5 words are still missed after this scaffolded round, repeat word-builder/visual-explainer before independent checkpoint.
measurement.falsifyCriteria: Scaffolded letter-box recall is not independent mastery evidence; retry and letter-tile support are present as contamination risks.

spelling.reason: Targets the 4 missed words plus 'sunny' which had no scoreable response (not_sure) on baseline discovery.
spelling.uncertainty: Scaffolded recall with letter boxes and hidden word; supportive but not unaided.

measurement.supportCriteria: Guided letter-build mode with letter bank support and up to 2 retries, audio or visible prompt, for the same 5 target words.
measurement.reviseCriteria: If child needs max retries on 3+ words, loop back to visual-explainer chunk teaching for those words.
measurement.falsifyCriteria: Guided/supported construction with retries is practice evidence only, not proof of unaided recall.

spelling.reason: Second practice pass on same weak-word set to build construction fluency before timed/puzzle practice and the final checkpoint.
spelling.uncertainty: Letter-bank and retry support reduce task difficulty; not independent evidence.

measurement.supportCriteria: Targeted recovery run ordering misses first across the full 20-word list for fast, engaging retrieval fluency practice.
measurement.reviseCriteria: Not used to revise teaching; purely fluency and confidence building after targeted instruction.
measurement.falsifyCriteria: Visible-word and retry contamination risks mean this cannot serve as independent recall evidence.

spelling.reason: Builds speed and confidence across the whole word list with the weak words resurfaced first via misses-first ordering.
spelling.uncertainty: Speed/arcade format with visible-word elements; engagement and practice only.

measurement.supportCriteria: Trap-the-imposter mode with near-miss distractors across the full word list, word hidden, for visual discrimination practice.
measurement.reviseCriteria: Not used alone to revise; pairs with other practice evidence for the full-list pattern.
measurement.falsifyCriteria: Multiple-choice discrimination among near-miss distractors is diagnostic for visual discrimination, not unaided production.

spelling.reason: Provides speed-pressure discrimination practice distinguishing correct spellings from near-miss errors similar to Sunny's actual miss patterns (slowle, quickle, commne, remembre).
spelling.uncertainty: Multiple-choice format differs from free recall; diagnostic for discrimination only.

measurement.supportCriteria: Constrained-guess puzzle format reasoning through letter position for the 5 weak words.
measurement.reviseCriteria: If child cannot narrow guesses using feedback after 2 words, pair with more visual-explainer chunk review.
measurement.falsifyCriteria: Hint and retry contamination mean this is practice-level evidence of strategy, not unaided recall proof.

spelling.reason: Alternative engaging practice format reinforcing letter-position awareness on the same weak-word set.
spelling.uncertainty: Puzzle feedback loop provides scaffolding; not independent recall.

measurement.supportCriteria: Pattern-inference mode using homework words with limited hints and a companion opponent for engagement.
measurement.reviseCriteria: Not used alone to revise; pairs with other practice evidence.
measurement.falsifyCriteria: Reward/preference-oriented format with hint support; preference-only proof strength, not recall evidence.

spelling.reason: Alternative engaging practice format reinforcing the same weak-word set via pattern inference instead of arcade speed.
spelling.uncertainty: Preference/reward-oriented activity; low proof strength for recall.

measurement.supportCriteria: Cold recall mode: audio-or-definition prompt, word hidden, zero retries, captured response, across all 20 assigned words.
measurement.reviseCriteria: Any word missed here should return to word-radar hidden_word_recall or spell-check audio_prompt_spell practice before the real test, not be treated as failure.
measurement.falsifyCriteria: This checkpoint is the fresh, unaided production evidence required by the readiness proof standard; it is diagnostic, not a mastery or readiness declaration.

spelling.reason: Re-measures independent unaided spelling across all 20 assigned words after targeted instruction and varied practice on the previously missed/uncertain items (slowly, quickly, common, remember, sunny), matching the central readiness question: can Sunny spell the test words from memory without seeing them.
spelling.uncertainty: Single-occasion measurement; does not confirm delayed retention toward the actual test date, which is currently unknown.

planTheory.hypothesis: Sunny has largely mastered the -y/-ly adverb/adjective pattern (15 of 20 words correct on independent discovery) but has specific gaps in 4 words (slowly, quickly, common, remember) plus one unscored item (sunny) that need direct chunk instruction and repeated scaffolded-to-independent practice before the real spelling test.
evidenceSummary: Discovery baseline (20/20 attempted, independent, unaided, word hidden) shows 15 words spelled correctly on first unaided try: shiny, lucky, neatly, likely, messy, rainy, friendly, able, behind, carefully, easy, fact, sure, vowel, whole.

4 words were independently missed with consistent, interpretable error patterns: slowly->slowle (dropped final y), quickly->quickle (dropped final y), common->commne (letter transposition/doubling confusion), remember->remembre (letter-order/final-cluster confusion).
1 word (sunny) produced no scoreable response (child marked not_sure), so its status is genuinely unknown rather than wrong.
No prior recentEvidence exists for this child, so this discovery pass is the establishing baseline, not a confirmation of a known pattern.
planTheory.intervention: Teach the specific orthographic chunks underlying the 4 missed words via visual-explainer, then move through two scaffolded practice passes (word-radar partial recall with letter boxes, spell-check guided letter build) targeting those words plus 'sunny', then offer a motivating choice between arcade-speed practice (monster-stampede, letter-rush) and puzzle-strategy practice (wordle, wheel-of-fortune) covering the same weak set plus full-list fluency, and finish with an independent cold-recall spell-check checkpoint across all 20 words as the fresh, unaided measurement of current standing relative to the test.
supportCriteria: Direct chunk teaching is provided only for the words with documented independent errors or unknown status, not the 15 already-correct words.
Practice activities use scaffolds (letter boxes, letter banks, limited retries) appropriate to difficulty before removing support.

The choice point offers two independently valid practice wrappers (arcade vs puzzle) covering identical target words and skill, preserving academic equivalence while letting engagement preference drive selection.
reviseCriteria: If the independent checkpoint still shows the same 4-5 words missed, revise the plan to add another visual-explainer + word-builder scaffolding cycle focused specifically on those words before the real test.
If new words beyond the original 5 appear missed at checkpoint, treat as new evidence requiring expanded targeted instruction, not a discipline issue.
falsifyCriteria: If the final cold-recall checkpoint shows accuracy at or below the original baseline (15/20) despite the added instruction and practice, the chunk-teaching hypothesis for those specific errors is not supported and should be revised (e.g., consider auditory discrimination or motor/typing confounds instead).

If 'sunny' is answered correctly at checkpoint, the not_sure baseline response was likely uncertainty/confidence-related rather than a true knowledge gap, and future planning should not treat it as an error pattern.
